_comment: Editor layout for LifetimeMixtureModel. The standard TCSPC nuisance groups are inherited; the Mixture panel drives the fit-selection and fraction controls via the custom fit_mixer section. Keep the Convolution/Generic/Corrections panels in step with lifetime.view.json -- they describe the same nuisance groups, and a control added to only one of them is a parity gap between two editors a user reads as the same.

sections.title: Convolution

sections.label: Type
sections.description: Excitation scheme for the IRF convolution.
descriptions: Periodic excitation: the decay wraps around the repetition period (pulsed laser, tails overlap).
Single excitation, truncated at the histogram window; no wrap-around.
Full (numpy) convolution of one excitation with the model, without wrap-around.

sections.label: Convolve
sections.description: Convolve the model with the IRF. Switch off to compare the bare decay.
Convolution of the model decay with the instrument response function (IRF): IRF curve, excitation mode, convolve switch and IRF time shift.

sections.title: Generic
sections.description: Nuisance terms of the decay: scattered light, constant background (and its curve) and photon counts.

sections.title: Corrections

sections.label: Smoothing
sections.description: Window used to smooth the linearization (DNL) table before it is applied; flat = no smoothing.

items.label: Pile-up
items.description: Correct pile-up distortion of the TCSPC histogram (early photons over-represented at high count rates).

items.label: DNL
items.description: Apply the differential non-linearity (DNL) table to the model to account for uneven channel widths.

items.label: Reverse
items.description: Reverse the time axis of the data (for reverse start-stop acquisition).

sections.description: Switches for the amplitude normalisation of the species.
Detector corrections: DNL linearization table, pile-up and channel smoothing applied to the decay.

sections.title: Mixture

sections.description: Select existing lifetime fits, add them with mixing fractions, and double-click a row to remove it.
Mixture of independent decay components; the fractions give the relative amplitude of each.
